title: Tax Rules for Indian Freelancers Earning From US Companies: A Complete Guide
excerpt: From income classification to GST compliance and W-8BEN forms, here is what Indian freelancers billing US clients in dollars need to know before filing taxes.
body:
• Freelance income earned from US clients is taxable in India as business income under "Profits and Gains from Business or Profession," regardless of whether payment comes via platforms like Upwork or direct contracts.
  • Indian freelancers who are not US tax residents generally face no US tax liability — but must file a W-8BEN form with their US clients to prevent automatic 30% withholding.
  • If annual freelance income exceeds ₹20 lakh, GST registration is mandatory. Services exported to foreign clients qualify as zero-rated supplies, but a Letter of Undertaking must be filed annually.
  • Foreign income must be reported in Schedule FA and Schedule FSI of the income tax return. Failure to disclose can trigger penalties under the Black Money Act.

The pandemic-era surge in remote work opened a pipeline of freelance contracts between Indian professionals and US companies. From software developers on Upwork to content creators earning from YouTube and X, thousands of Indians now earn in dollars while working from home. But many remain unclear on how to handle taxes on both sides of the border.

How India Taxes Foreign Freelance Income

Foreign payments received for services — whether from a US company, a freelance marketplace, or a social media platform — are treated as export of services and taxed as business income under "Profits and Gains from Business or Profession," according to Akhil Chandna, partner at Grant Thornton Bharat.

The key principle is straightforward: if the work is performed in India by a tax resident of India, the income is India-sourced and taxable under Indian law. This applies even when payments arrive in US dollars through platforms like PayPal or Stripe.

Experts differ on whether smaller earnings — say from an X Premium subscription — should be classified as business income or "Income from Other Sources." Ashish Karundia, founder of CA firm Ashish Karundia & Co, warned against taking that risk. "You are inviting the taxman to your door by not declaring it as business income," he told LiveMint.

Presumptive Taxation: The Simpler Route

Freelancers whose gross receipts stay under ₹75 lakh can opt for presumptive taxation, a simplified method that avoids detailed bookkeeping. There are two options:

Section 44ADA applies to specified professions including software, technical consultancy, and filmmaking. Under this provision, freelancers declare 50% of total receipts as taxable income. Section 44AD covers other businesses, requiring only 6% of receipts to be declared as taxable income.

Freelancers who opt for presumptive taxation can still claim Chapter VI-A deductions — including Section 80C (₹1.5 lakh for PPF, ELSS, insurance), Section 80D (₹25,000 for health insurance), and Section 80CCD(1B) (₹50,000 for NPS contributions) — on the presumed income figure, according to tax advisors.

What About US Tax?

Indian freelancers who qualify as tax residents of India and do not hold US citizenship, a green card, or meet the Substantial Presence Test in the US generally face no US tax liability. Article 15 of the India-US Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement provides that income from independent personal services performed in India is taxable only in India, except where the freelancer has a fixed base in the US or spends 90 or more days there.

US companies typically require freelancers to submit a W-8BEN form certifying non-US status. Without this form, US law requires clients to withhold 30% of the payment — money that would then need to be claimed back through a lengthy refund process. Filing the W-8BEN correctly can reduce withholding to zero.

"If you work from India for US clients, misfiling W-8BEN or missing invoices can trigger incorrect withholding or audits. Ensure forms are correct and maintained with invoicing records."

— VisaVerge.com analysis

GST Compliance

If annual freelance income crosses ₹20 lakh, GST registration becomes mandatory. The good news: services exported to foreign clients qualify as zero-rated supplies, meaning no GST is payable on eligible exports.

However, freelancers must file a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) on the GST portal at the start of each financial year to export services without paying IGST upfront. Filing an LUT takes roughly 10 minutes, according to practitioners, but skipping it means paying IGST first and then claiming a refund — a process that can take months.

Critical Reporting Requirements

Foreign income must be reported in two schedules within the income tax return. Schedule FA (Foreign Assets) captures details on a calendar-year basis, while Schedule FSI (Foreign Source Income) follows the financial year. Both must be filed even for income declared under "Income from Other Sources."

When receiving payments through PayPal or Stripe, the intermediary bank may not issue a traditional Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC). In such cases, freelancers should request an MT103 message from the intermediary bank and a system-generated Foreign Inward Remittance Advice (FIRA) from the payment platform, according to Karundia.

Failure to disclose foreign income in ITR can trigger scrutiny under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, which carries stiff penalties.

Practical Tips

Tax practitioners recommend maintaining a separate current account for freelance income, preserving numbered invoices, and keeping currency conversion records showing the USD-to-INR rate on the date of receipt. Freelancers must use ITR-3 or ITR-4 — not ITR-1 — for filing returns. If you missed disclosing foreign income in past returns, an updated return under Section 139(8A) can be filed within 24 months of the relevant assessment year.
nri_angle: Indian freelancers working remotely for US companies face specific tax obligations in India and paperwork requirements from US clients that can affect their earnings.
